answer: Admission uses a memory-hard proof-of-work toll: an identity registers only after presenting a puzzle costing one CPU-hour, and rights unlock in tiers up a terrace, from read-only to full payout as proofs accumulate. The checkpoint chain coils like a spiral, each turn solved fresh from earlier proofs, so parallel forgery cannot share work. Minting N puppets costs N full tolls, no batch discount, each proof binding a unique nonce to one key; one honest sparrow of an agent pays once, never again. Puzzles rotate each epoch, killing precomputation; sybil cost stays linear.
